newsitem.title: USA: Aeroflot mulls flower freighter ex-Miami.
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot mulls flower freighter ex-Miami.

text.p: Demand for imported flowers is so great in Russia that Aeroflot Airlines is mulling adding a freighter through Miami International Airport, an Aeroflot executive told Reuters Tuesday.
"It is a good solid market," said Robert McKay, Aeroflot's southeastern regional director of marketing and sales.
If the company decides the demand is sufficient inbound to Miami, Aeroflot would like to start the freighter sometime this quarter, McKay said.
Flowers going to Russia are primarily from Ecuador.

Demand for the fresh cut flowers currently outstrips Aeroflot's belly capacity on passenger flights, McKay said. Aeroflot offers the only non-stop service from Miami and the flowers suffer when aircraft stop in Europe on route to Moscow.

Aeroflot is changing its U.S. fleet to widebody from narrow body aircraft, McKay said. However, since it is reducing its MIA service from five to two weekly flights, belly capacity will be little changed.
